sentences.text: 30. Heard the submission.

Perused the record of the Ld. Trial Court and also perused the impugned order of Ld. Trial Court dated 21.03.2024.
31.

The revisionist/complainant has approached to this Court against the impugned order dated 21.03.2024 vide which Ld. Trial Court had declined to summon the respondents/accused persons with respect to the commission of offence punishable U/s 417/419/420/467/468/471/474 IPC.
32.

It is the contention of the revisionist/complainant that respondents had committed the offence of cheating as punishable U/s 417 IPC, the offence of personation and offence of cheating and dishonestly inducing the delivery of property as punishable U/s 419 IPC and as punishable U/s 420 IPC.

32.1 It is also the contention of the revisionist/complainant that accused/respondents had committed the offence punishable U/s 467 IPC for forgery of valuable security and offence punishable U/s 468 IPC of forgery for purpose of cheating.

It is also contention of the revisionist/complainant that accused persons had committed the offence punishable U/s 471 IPC for using as genuine a forged document and offence punishable U/s 474 IPC for having possession of document described U/s 467 IPC, knowing it to be forged and intending to use it as genuine.

32.2 As per its own case of the revisionist/complainant, the loan was sanctioned and agreement for the loan was executed in pursuance to the agreement of loan on 16.04.2023 and the loan amount was credited to the account of respondent no. 2 firm.

Date: 2025.10.08 PANDEY 16:06:38 +0530 instead of crediting it to the dealer of the showroom from where the vehicle was purchased.

It is also admitted fact that the accused had made the payment of loan installments/EMIs amount upto the year 2017 and thereafter, the accused had stopped making payment of the loan amount installments.

Hence,
there was a lapse on the part of duty of the bank officials who credited the loan amount in the account of the firm of the accused instead of crediting it in the account of the showroom/shop from where the vehicle was purchased.

The bank officials had never insisted to obtain the permanent registration number of the vehicle from the accused persons and nor get the vehicle hypothecation entered against its registration number with the Registration Authorities.

It cannot be inferred that there was element of cheating from the beginning i.e. from the date of the execution of loan agreement between the bank and the accused persons as accused persons had made the payment of loan installment amount upto the year 2017.

32.4 The evidence as led on behalf of the revisionist bank through the witness CW1 failed to prima facie show that any offence as alleged punishable U/s 417/419/420/467/468/471/474 IPC or any other offence was committed by the accused persons against the complainant/revisionist bank and the dispute between the parties was of civil nature regarding the recovery of loan amount from the respondents by the complainant/revisionist bank.

The Court is of the view that there is no illegality or infirmity in the order of Ld. Trial Court vide which it was observed that no prima facie case was made out to proceed against the accused persons for commission of offence punishable U/s 417/419/420/467/468/471/474 IPC.
Hence, the revision petition of the revisionist/complainant bank does not hold any merit and accordingly dismissed.
